courses.title: Essential Commands
courses.description: Teach fundamental commands every puppy needs.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Name Recognition
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to respond promptly and consistently to their name.
steps: Gather Treats: Prepare small, tasty treats your puppy loves.
Quiet Environment: Start in a quiet area without distractions.
Say the Name Clearly: Clearly call your puppy’s name in a happy, gentle tone.
Reward Attention: As soon as your puppy looks at you, immediately reward them with a treat and praise (“Good job!”).
Repeat Regularly: Practice short sessions (3–5 mins) several times a day.
tips: Always keep your voice friendly and inviting.
Never use the puppy’s name negatively or during corrections.
lessons.completionCriteria: Your puppy consistently turns toward you when called 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Sit Command
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to reliably sit on cue with simple, effective steps.
steps: Prepare Reward: Have treats ready in your hand.
Attract Attention: Let your puppy see and smell the treat in your hand.
Lure Into Sitting: Slowly move the treat from your puppy's nose upward and slightly over their head, guiding them into a natural sitting position.
Immediate Reward: When your puppy’s rear touches the ground, say clearly “Sit!”, then immediately give the treat and praise.
Repeat the Cue: Repeat several times until your puppy consistently sits with minimal guidance.
tips: Keep training sessions brief (3–5 mins each session).
Gradually reduce hand gestures until only the verbal cue is needed.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy consistently sits promptly upon hearing the “Sit” command at least 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Lie Down
lessons.goal: Encourage your puppy to calmly lie down on cue and remain relaxed.
steps: Begin from Sitting: Get your puppy into the sitting position first.
Lure Downward: Take a treat, hold it close to your puppy’s nose, then slowly move the treat downward toward the ground, guiding them into a lying position.
Praise and Reward: The moment your puppy’s elbows touch the floor, clearly say “Down!” and reward immediately.
Practice Regularly: Repeat multiple short sessions, gradually reducing the treat guidance.
tips: Avoid forcing or pressing your puppy into the down position.
Be patient—some puppies take longer to feel comfortable lying down.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy reliably lies down within seconds of hearing the command “Down” 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Stay Command
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy patience, self-control, and reliability by holding a position until released.
steps: Begin with “Sit”: Command your puppy into the sit position first.
Use Clear Signal: Hold up your open hand clearly in front of your puppy’s face and calmly say “Stay.”
Short Duration: Initially wait just 2–3 seconds, then say “OK” or “Free,” release the puppy and reward immediately.
Gradually Extend: Slowly increase the duration and distance, stepping back while your puppy remains seated.
tips: Always clearly release your puppy before they move.
Move slowly to avoid overwhelming your puppy.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy remains reliably in place (sit or down) for at least 15–20 seconds, with mild distractions, 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Come When Called
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to reliably return to you immediately when called, ensuring their safety.
steps: Choose Your Cue: Use a friendly, inviting voice to call your puppy clearly, e.g., “Come!” or “Here!”
Short Distance Practice: Begin indoors from short distances (3–5 feet). Call your puppy enthusiastically, then reward instantly with treats and praise when they come.
Increase Distance Gradually: Once your puppy reliably responds, increase distance and try calling from another room.
Introduce Mild Distractions: After consistent responses indoors, practice outdoors with minimal distractions.
tips: Always reward your puppy generously when they respond.
Never punish or scold your puppy after they come to you.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy reliably returns promptly upon hearing your recall command 8 out of 10 times from varying short distances.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Walking Nicely on a Leash
lessons.goal: Help your puppy learn to walk calmly at your side, preventing leash pulling.
steps: Introduce the Leash: Let your puppy sniff and get comfortable with the leash before starting.
Start Indoors or Quiet Area: With the leash loose, start walking slowly. Reward your puppy for staying close.
Stop When Pulling Occurs: If your puppy pulls, immediately stop walking. Wait until your puppy relaxes, then continue.
Change Direction Frequently: Make frequent gentle turns, encouraging your puppy’s focus on you.
tips: Keep initial training sessions brief and positive (5–10 minutes).
Use small treats or praise frequently to reinforce good behavior.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy consistently walks beside you on a loose leash without pulling, maintaining focus for at least 10 consecutive steps, 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Leave It
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to ignore tempting but unwanted items on command, improving safety and impulse control.
steps: Start with Treats: Place a treat in your closed fist. Let your puppy sniff but say “Leave it” firmly.
Reward for Compliance: As soon as your puppy stops sniffing or looks away, praise and give a different treat from your other hand.
Open-Hand Challenge: Progress to placing a treat openly on your palm and repeat the “Leave it” command.
Floor Test: Place a treat on the floor, cover it initially with your hand, gradually exposing it while reinforcing the “Leave it” cue.
tips: Reinforce generously when your puppy successfully ignores the item.
Stay patient and consistent, avoiding frustration or punishment.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy reliably ignores or looks away from tempting items when hearing “Leave it” at least 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Drop It
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to willingly release items on command, facilitating safer interactions and preventing possessiveness.
steps: Engage in Gentle Play: Offer your puppy a toy they enjoy, gently engaging in play.
Introduce the “Drop it” Cue: Clearly and calmly say “Drop it,” showing a tasty treat as a trade.
Immediate Reward: As soon as your puppy releases the toy, reward immediately with praise and the treat.
Repeat Frequently: Repeat with different toys, slowly phasing out the food lure, rewarding intermittently with praise.
tips: Never forcibly remove items from your puppy’s mouth; instead, patiently encourage voluntary release.
Use valuable rewards initially, gradually reducing their frequency.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy promptly releases items from their mouth on hearing “Drop it” command at least 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Wait at Doors
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to calmly wait at doors until you give permission, promoting safe and polite behavior.
steps: Approach the Door: Walk your puppy on a leash toward a closed door. Stop about 2 feet away.
Ask for a Sit: Give a clear “Sit” command. Once your puppy sits, praise calmly.
Introduce “Wait” Command: Clearly say “Wait” and slowly begin to open the door. If your puppy moves, gently close the door and repeat.
Allow Passage: When your puppy calmly waits as the door opens, say “Okay!” or “Let’s go!” and calmly move through together.
tips: Initially practice at internal doors before trying exterior doors.
Be patient and consistent, rewarding generously for calm behavior.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy reliably waits calmly at doors until given permission to pass, successfully 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Gentle Greetings
lessons.goal: Prevent your puppy from jumping up by teaching polite, calm greetings to family and visitors.
steps: Controlled Setup: Start with your puppy on a leash. Have someone approach calmly to greet.
Reinforce Sit: As the person approaches, instruct your puppy clearly to “Sit.”
Reward Calmness: If your puppy remains sitting and calm, praise immediately and allow gentle greeting interaction.
Manage Jumping: If your puppy jumps, the greeter should calmly step back and ignore the puppy until calm again.
tips: Ensure every greeting is calm; high-energy greetings reinforce jumping.
Gradually practice with more distractions or increased excitement levels.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy consistently remains seated or standing calmly without jumping when greeting people, achieving success in 8 out of 10 greetings.

courses.title: Potty Training Success
courses.description: Quick methods to house-train your puppy.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Setting a Routine
lessons.goal: Establish a clear and predictable potty schedule for your puppy, encouraging consistent habits.
steps: Identify Key Times: Observe when your puppy typically needs to go—after waking, playing, meals, or drinking water.
Create a Schedule: Write down specific potty times based on these observations (e.g., every 1–2 hours initially).
Consistent Implementation: Follow the schedule strictly for several days, ensuring you guide your puppy outdoors at scheduled times.
Reward Success: Praise and reward immediately every time your puppy eliminates outdoors as planned.
tips: Adjust the schedule gradually as your puppy grows and their bladder control improves.
Keep the routine consistent every day to accelerate learning.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy consistently follows the established potty schedule with minimal accidents over 2–3 consecutive days.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Choosing a Potty Spot
lessons.goal: Teach your puppy to consistently use a specific, designated area outdoors for potty breaks.
steps: Pick a Specific Spot: Select a convenient outdoor area as the dedicated potty zone.
Guide Your Puppy: Consistently take your puppy directly to this spot during scheduled potty breaks.
Use a Cue Word: When you arrive at the spot, use a consistent verbal cue such as “Go potty.”
Praise and Reward: Reward enthusiastically immediately after successful potty behavior at the spot.
tips: Use a leash initially to guide your puppy directly to the spot.
Avoid play or distractions in the potty area to reinforce the specific purpose.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy reliably goes potty in the chosen location when guided, at least 8 out of 10 potty breaks.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Recognizing Potty Signals
lessons.goal: Learn to identify your puppy’s unique signals and body language indicating they need to potty.
steps: Careful Observation: Closely watch your puppy to notice signals like sniffing, circling, restlessness, or whining.
Take Notes: Keep a brief record of signals and corresponding potty breaks.
Prompt Response: When you notice these signals, immediately guide your puppy to the designated potty area.
Consistent Reinforcement: Reward and praise your puppy for successfully signaling and using the potty spot.
tips: Each puppy has unique signals; attentive observation helps identify these quickly.
Quick responses reduce indoor accidents and accelerate training.
lessons.completionCriteria: You confidently recognize your puppy’s potty signals and act promptly, resulting in successful pottying outdoors 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Positive Reinforcement
lessons.goal: Use rewards effectively to encourage and reinforce proper potty habits.
steps: Prepare Rewards: Keep small, high-value treats ready near your potty spot.
Immediate Reward: Immediately reward your puppy after successfully pottying in the correct area, accompanied by enthusiastic praise.
Verbal Praise: Use consistent positive phrases like “Good potty!” each time.
Consistent Repetition: Repeat rewarding consistently every time the desired behavior occurs, gradually phasing out treats as habits form.
tips: Rewards should be immediate for your puppy to make the correct association.
Maintain enthusiasm and consistency to strengthen learning.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy associates pottying outside with rewards and praise consistently, responding positively at least 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Handling Accidents
lessons.goal: Effectively manage indoor potty accidents, minimizing frustration and reinforcing correct behavior.
steps: Remain Calm: If an accident occurs indoors, remain calm and avoid scolding.
Immediate Response: Interrupt gently if you catch your puppy in the act, quickly guiding them outdoors to finish.
Effective Cleaning: Thoroughly clean accident areas using an enzymatic cleaner to eliminate odors and discourage repeat incidents.
Review Routine: Evaluate and adjust your potty schedule or watch more closely for signals if accidents persist.
tips: Never punish after the fact; your puppy won’t understand and may become anxious.
Focus on positive reinforcement to reduce future accidents.
lessons.completionCriteria: Indoor accidents noticeably reduced; puppy consistently redirected outside at least 8 out of 10 times after minor setbacks.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Nighttime Potty Training
lessons.goal: Develop an effective nighttime potty routine to minimize overnight accidents and encourage longer sleep intervals.
steps: Adjust Feeding and Watering: Limit water intake 1–2 hours before bedtime, and schedule the last potty break right before sleep.
Set Alarms: Initially, set a nighttime alarm to take your puppy out for a brief potty break midway through the night.
Minimize Nighttime Interaction: Keep nighttime outings quiet, calm, and brief, avoiding play to indicate it’s sleep time.
Gradually Extend Sleep Periods: Slowly increase intervals between nighttime potty breaks as bladder control improves.
tips: Consistency and calmness during night breaks help your puppy understand expectations.
Patience is key; improvement usually happens gradually.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy sleeps through most of the night (6–8 hours) without accidents consistently over several consecutive nights.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Crate Training Integration
lessons.goal: Incorporate crate training to effectively speed up potty training success and manage potty breaks efficiently.
steps: Introduce the Crate Positively: Gradually introduce your puppy to the crate with treats and comfortable bedding.
Routine Crating: Use the crate for short periods when you cannot supervise, as puppies naturally avoid pottying where they sleep.
Scheduled Potty Breaks: Consistently let your puppy out to potty immediately upon removal from the crate.
Positive Association: Reward puppy immediately after pottying successfully outdoors following crate time.
tips: Crate should never be used as punishment.
Gradually extend crate time as puppy adapts comfortably.
lessons.completionCriteria: Puppy consistently keeps crate clean, with accidents reduced to nearly zero over multiple days of consistent crate usage.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Troubleshooting Challenges
lessons.goal: Identify, address, and overcome common potty training issues and setbacks.
steps: Identify Issues: Note specific problems (e.g., regression, frequent indoor accidents, refusal to potty outdoors).
Assess Routine: Review the current schedule, rewards system, and potty spot conditions for improvements.
Make Adjustments: Modify training methods, increase frequency of breaks, improve reward quality, or reassess crate usage.
Consistency and Patience: Persist with positive reinforcement, and calmly reinforce good habits to resolve setbacks effectively.
tips: Avoid becoming frustrated; setbacks are common and manageable.
Be flexible and ready to adjust training methods as needed.
lessons.completionCriteria: Common training issues resolved; puppy consistently demonstrates improved potty habits with few setbacks for at least 3–5 consecutive days.

courses.title: Basic Obedience
courses.description: Build foundational skills for good behavior.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Eye Contact
lessons.goal: Strengthen your dog's attention and communication by teaching focused eye contact on cue.
steps: Prepare Rewards: Hold small, tasty treats near your face.
Gain Attention: Clearly say your dog's name and wait until they look directly at your eyes.
Immediate Reward: Instantly praise ("Yes!" or "Good!") and reward when eye contact occurs.
Gradually Extend Duration: Slowly increase the length of eye contact required before rewarding.
tips: Always keep your voice gentle and encouraging.
Frequent short sessions yield the best results.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably holds eye contact for at least 5 seconds upon hearing their name in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Sit-Stay Basics
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to remain seated calmly until explicitly released.
steps: Give Sit Command: Instruct your dog to "Sit", rewarding immediately when sitting occurs.
Introduce Stay Command: With your open palm toward your dog, say "Stay" calmly.
Brief Stay Duration: Initially, keep the stay short (2–3 seconds). Reward instantly and clearly release with a cue like "OK."
Increase Time Gradually: Slowly increase the duration of the stay, rewarding consistently.
tips: If your dog moves prematurely, simply guide them back gently without scolding.
Regularly practice short sessions daily.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably remains seated for at least 15–20 seconds until released, 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Down-Stay Fundamentals
lessons.goal: Establish foundational skills for your dog to remain calmly lying down until released.
steps: Begin with Down: Command your dog into a "Down" position first, reward immediately.
Introduce Stay Cue: Clearly give the command "Stay," using a calm, firm voice and an open-hand signal.
Short Initial Stays: Wait 2–3 seconds initially, then release and reward generously.
Extend Stay Gradually: Gradually increase both duration and distance while maintaining consistency.
tips: Keep sessions short and positive, avoiding frustration or fatigue.
Reward generously and consistently.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently holds a down-stay calmly for 20–30 seconds, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Come When Called
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to reliably return to you when called in various everyday situations.
steps: Pick Your Cue: Use a clear, enthusiastic cue like "Come!" or "Here!"
Short-Distance Recall: Start indoors or in a quiet area at short distances (2–3 meters).
Reward Instantly: Immediately praise and reward generously when your dog arrives.
Practice Regularly: Gradually introduce minor distractions as recall improves.
tips: Never call your dog to punish them; ensure recall always results in positive outcomes.
Regular, short sessions enhance reliability.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently returns immediately upon hearing the recall command 8 out of 10 times, even with minor distractions.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Loose Leash Walking
lessons.goal: Train your dog to walk calmly at your side without pulling on the leash.
steps: Start Calmly: Begin leash training indoors or in a quiet, familiar outdoor area.
Reward Proper Position: Encourage your dog to stay close to your side. Reward immediately for maintaining position without pulling.
Stop-and-Go Technique: If your dog pulls, calmly stop walking. Wait until the leash loosens, then continue.
Directional Changes: Frequently change directions to encourage your dog’s attention on you.
tips: Keep initial sessions short (5–10 minutes) and positive.
Consistency and patience are critical; reward generously for calm behavior.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently walks calmly beside you on a loose leash for at least 10 consecutive steps, successfully in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Wait at Doors and Gates
lessons.goal: Encourage your dog to pause and wait politely at doors and gates until given permission to pass through safely.
steps: Approach and Stop: Walk your dog on-leash toward a closed door or gate. Stop approximately 1–2 feet away.
Cue "Wait": Calmly give the command "Wait" while raising your hand as a visual signal.
Open Door Slowly: Gradually open the door or gate slightly. If your dog moves forward prematurely, gently close the door and repeat.
Release Command: When your dog waits calmly, give a clear release cue like "Okay!" or "Let’s go!" and proceed through together.
tips: Consistency is crucial—practice at various doors and gates regularly.
Keep your demeanor calm to reinforce patient behavior.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably waits at doors or gates until released 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Leave It Command
lessons.goal: Train your dog to reliably ignore or turn away from tempting but inappropriate items on command.
steps: Present Temptation: Hold a treat or object in your closed fist, allowing your dog to sniff but not take it.
Cue "Leave it": Clearly and firmly say "Leave it" and wait until your dog stops trying to reach the object.
Reward Correct Behavior: Once your dog looks away or pauses, immediately reward from your other hand with praise and a different treat.
Increase Difficulty: Gradually practice with open-hand temptations and floor-level items.
tips: Always reward promptly and generously when your dog successfully ignores the item.
Gradually increase distractions as your dog’s skills improve.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently leaves tempting items when given the "Leave it" command in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Drop Items on Cue
lessons.goal: Develop reliable responses from your dog to release items gently and immediately upon command.
steps: Initiate Play: Offer your dog a toy they enjoy holding or playing with.
Introduce Cue: Calmly and clearly say "Drop it," simultaneously offering a high-value treat as an exchange.
Immediate Reward: Reward instantly with praise and the treat once your dog releases the object.
Practice Frequently: Regularly practice, eventually phasing out the food reward, using praise alone intermittently.
tips: Never forcibly remove items; encourage voluntary release gently.
Ensure rewards are consistently motivating initially.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog willingly releases items promptly upon hearing "Drop it" in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Polite Greetings
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to greet people calmly without jumping or excessive excitement.
steps: Set Up Controlled Greetings: Have a helper calmly approach your dog while the dog is leashed.
Encourage Calmness: Command your dog to sit as the helper approaches. Reward immediately for calm sitting behavior.
Discourage Jumping: If your dog jumps, have the helper calmly turn away and ignore until your dog sits or remains calm again.
Consistent Repetition: Regularly practice with multiple people and gradually increase excitement levels.
tips: Always reward calm greetings immediately.
Avoid reinforcing jumping by ignoring excited greetings.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently greets people calmly without jumping in 8 out of 10 encounters.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Place Command
lessons.goal: Train your dog to relax calmly on a designated spot (such as a mat or bed) upon command.
steps: Choose a Spot: Pick a comfortable mat or dog bed as the designated place.
Guide to Place: Use a treat to guide your dog onto the mat. Once all four paws are on, say clearly "Place."
Reward Calmness: Encourage your dog to lie down calmly, immediately rewarding the calm position with praise and treats.
Extend Duration: Gradually increase the time your dog remains on their place before releasing them with a cue such as "Free" or "Okay."
tips: Keep the place spot consistent initially to reinforce understanding.
Reward generously and frequently at first, gradually reducing frequency over time.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably goes to their designated place on cue and remains calmly for at least 30 seconds, 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Handling and Grooming
lessons.goal: Make grooming and physical handling stress-free and comfortable for your dog.
steps: Introduce Tools: Let your dog calmly sniff grooming tools (brush, comb, nail clippers).
Gentle Touch: Briefly and gently touch paws, ears, and mouth areas, rewarding immediately for calm acceptance.
Positive Grooming: Slowly introduce gentle brushing or combing, pairing each action with treats and praise.
Build Duration: Gradually extend grooming time as your dog remains comfortable and calm.
tips: Keep initial sessions short, positive, and frequent.
Stop immediately if your dog becomes stressed and resume later with shorter steps.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog calmly allows basic grooming and handling for at least 5 consecutive minutes without resistance.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Stay with Distractions
lessons.goal: Strengthen your dog’s “stay” command even when faced with mild to moderate distractions.
steps: Start Simple: Give the “stay” command in a familiar, quiet location initially.
Introduce Minor Distractions: Begin introducing mild distractions (e.g., gently tossing a toy nearby) while maintaining a stay.
Reward and Reinforce: Immediately reward calm staying behavior and gradually increase distraction levels.
Consistency: Regularly practice in various settings, increasing distractions slowly.
tips: Gradually increase distraction intensity; ensure success before moving forward.
Use high-value rewards to reinforce staying despite distractions.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently holds a stay for 20–30 seconds amidst moderate distractions in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 13: Controlled Play
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to engage in safe, calm, and controlled play, preventing overly rough behaviors.
steps: Choose Appropriate Toys: Select toys your dog enjoys and can easily handle calmly.
Initiate Gentle Play: Start play sessions calmly, immediately pausing and withdrawing if play becomes too rough.
Introduce Cues: Clearly say "Easy" or "Gentle" if play escalates, rewarding calmer interactions immediately.
Consistent Reinforcement: Regularly reward calm and appropriate play behaviors.
tips: Always end play sessions on a calm, positive note.
Use brief play pauses to reinforce self-control.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog engages calmly in play sessions, responding promptly to calming cues in 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 14: Quiet Command
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to reduce barking effectively and reliably respond to a “quiet” cue.
steps: Trigger Controlled Barking: Use a mild trigger (doorbell knock) to prompt barking briefly.
Introduce Quiet Cue: Calmly but firmly say “Quiet,” rewarding immediately when your dog pauses barking.
Reward Silence: Provide consistent rewards during quiet moments, extending quiet durations progressively.
Increase Difficulty: Gradually practice with more challenging triggers or prolonged barking scenarios.
tips: Avoid shouting or excessive reactions; remain calm.
Reward generously for quick and sustained responses to the quiet command.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently stops barking promptly upon hearing the “Quiet” command in 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Review and Graduation
lessons.goal: Review and consolidate all obedience skills learned in previous lessons, confirming reliability and celebrating progress.
steps: Conduct Skill Review: Systematically practice all previously learned commands (Sit, Down, Stay, Come, etc.).
Test Reliability: Practice each command in a variety of settings and with minor distractions.
Reward Successes: Generously reward each correctly executed command to reinforce learning.
Celebrate Achievements: Finish with positive interactions, games, and extra praise to mark graduation.
tips: Be patient and supportive, especially with challenging commands.
Regularly revisit this review to maintain skills.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog confidently and reliably performs each learned command under moderate distraction, successfully completing at least 8 out of 10 command attempts.

courses.title: Intermediate Obedience
courses.description: Advance your dog's listening and attention.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Extended Stay
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to confidently hold a "stay" command for longer durations, even with mild distractions.
steps: Start Simple: Give your dog a clear "Stay" command from a sitting or down position.
Gradual Duration Increase: Begin with short intervals (5–10 seconds) and gradually increase the time.
Introduce Distractions: Add minor distractions such as stepping sideways or clapping softly from a distance.
Reward Consistency: Reward generously whenever your dog successfully holds position, gradually increasing the stay duration.
tips: Stay patient; increase distractions and duration slowly.
Regular short sessions yield the best progress.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably holds stay command for at least 45–60 seconds with mild distractions in 8 out of 10 trials.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Reliable Recall at Distance
lessons.goal: Build a reliable and immediate recall from your dog, even from greater distances.
steps: Start Short: Call your dog using the recall cue ("Come!") from short distances (5–10 feet) and reward immediately.
Gradually Increase Distance: Slowly extend the recall distance incrementally (up to 20–30 feet).
Varied Environments: Practice recall in different settings with minimal distractions, increasing gradually.
Consistent Rewarding: Reward every successful recall immediately with treats, praise, or play.
tips: Keep your recall tone cheerful and inviting.
Never use recall for negative experiences or corrections.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently returns immediately when called from a distance of 20–30 feet, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Heel Command Basics
lessons.goal: Introduce your dog to the formal "heel" position, walking calmly at your left side.
steps: Start from Standstill: Place your dog on your left side, leash loosely in your hand.
Use Clear Cue: Clearly say "Heel," and begin walking forward slowly.
Guide Position: Use treats to guide your dog into proper heel position—head aligned with your leg.
Immediate Reinforcement: Consistently reward your dog whenever they stay in correct heel position.
tips: Keep sessions short to maintain your dog’s focus and interest.
Gradually reduce guidance, transitioning from food lures to verbal praise.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably maintains correct heel position for 10–15 consecutive steps in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Attention Around Distractions
lessons.goal: Maintain your dog’s focus and attention even in busy or distracting environments.
steps: Basic Attention Cue: Start in a quiet area, call your dog’s name, rewarding eye contact immediately.
Introduce Mild Distractions: Gradually add distractions such as background noises, people, or mild movements.
Reward Focus: Consistently reward every instance your dog maintains or quickly regains attention.
Increase Difficulty: Slowly build toward busier environments or more intense distractions.
tips: Frequent practice in varied locations builds reliability.
Keep sessions brief and positive, avoiding frustration.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently maintains or quickly refocuses attention in mildly distracting situations 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Stand-Stay Command
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to hold a calm standing position ("stand-stay") on cue.
steps: Position Dog in Stand: Guide your dog gently into a standing position, reward immediately.
Introduce "Stay": Clearly say "Stay," with an open-hand gesture facing your dog.
Short Duration First: Initially practice short stays (3–5 seconds), gradually increasing duration.
Reward Stillness: Praise and reward your dog for holding a calm standing position consistently.
tips: Maintain calmness and patience during practice.
Slowly increase the length and difficulty of stand-stays over time.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably holds a calm stand-stay for at least 20–30 seconds upon command, 8 out of 10 trials.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Go to Bed Command
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to calmly settle on a designated spot or bed upon command.
steps: Select a Spot: Place a comfortable dog bed or mat in a consistent location.
Introduce the Cue: Guide your dog onto the bed using a treat, clearly saying "Go to bed."
Reward Calmness: Once your dog lies down calmly, immediately praise and reward generously.
Gradually Increase Duration: Slowly extend the time your dog stays calmly on the bed before giving a release cue ("Okay!" or "Free!").
tips: Consistency in using the same spot helps your dog learn faster.
Initially, reward generously to reinforce the behavior.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably settles calmly on their designated bed upon cue for at least 30–60 seconds, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Emergency Stop
lessons.goal: Train your dog to stop immediately and remain still when given an emergency stop cue, enhancing safety.
steps: Begin in Controlled Area: Practice in a secure environment, initially with your dog close by.
Introduce Command: Clearly give a sharp and distinctive verbal cue, such as "Stop!" or "Halt!"
Immediate Pause: When your dog stops, instantly reward generously with praise and treats.
Extend Distance: Gradually practice from further away, reinforcing immediate response each time.
tips: Use a distinctive, firm tone for clarity and quick response.
Regularly practice to maintain reliability.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog stops immediately and reliably upon hearing the emergency cue, 8 out of 10 times, even at a distance.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Off-Leash Obedience Introduction
lessons.goal: Begin teaching your dog obedience commands confidently without relying on a leash.
steps: Secure Environment: Start in a safe, enclosed area to ensure your dog’s safety.
Review Known Commands: Practice basic commands like "Sit," "Stay," and "Come" initially with a leash, then gradually without it.
Positive Reinforcement: Immediately reward your dog generously for obeying commands off-leash.
Increase Challenge: Gradually introduce mild distractions or slightly increased distances as reliability improves.
tips: Consistency and high-value rewards build confidence and responsiveness.
Regular practice sessions maintain reliability.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably performs basic commands off-leash successfully 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Greeting People Calmly Outdoors
lessons.goal: Train your dog to greet new people politely and calmly outdoors, without jumping or excessive excitement.
steps: Initial Calmness: Begin with your dog in a sitting position at your side outdoors.
Controlled Approach: Allow another person to approach slowly. Reward your dog immediately for remaining seated and calm.
Manage Excitement: If your dog begins to jump or act excited, the approaching person should pause and step back briefly.
Reinforce Proper Greeting: Consistently reward calm behavior, gradually increasing excitement and number of people approaching.
tips: Stay calm yourself to encourage calmness in your dog.
Regularly practice with different individuals to generalize the behavior.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently greets people calmly outdoors, successfully demonstrating polite behavior 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Ignoring Other Dogs
lessons.goal: Develop your dog’s ability to calmly ignore or remain neutral toward other dogs during walks or outdoor activities.
steps: Controlled Distance: Begin practicing at a safe, comfortable distance from other dogs.
Maintain Attention: Regularly reinforce eye contact and calm behavior with treats and praise when another dog appears.
Gradual Approach: Slowly decrease distance between your dog and others, continuously reinforcing calmness.
Redirect Attention: Quickly redirect your dog’s focus back to you using commands or treats if distracted.
tips: Consistent positive reinforcement encourages calmness and focus.
Increase proximity to other dogs very gradually to ensure success.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog remains calm, neutral, and focused on you when encountering other dogs, successfully completing 8 out of 10 encounters.

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Long-Distance Commands
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to reliably respond to commands given from longer distances, enhancing control in various situations.
steps: Begin Close: Practice basic commands (Sit, Down, Stay) at short distances first (3–5 feet).
Gradual Distance Increase: Slowly increase distance, clearly giving commands and rewarding immediately upon correct response.
Use Clear Signals: Pair verbal commands with consistent hand signals to reinforce understanding.
Regular Practice: Regularly practice at varying distances, gradually increasing up to 15–25 feet.
tips: Ensure your voice is clear and loud enough for your dog to hear comfortably.
Always reward generously, reinforcing correct responses positively.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably responds to basic obedience commands at distances of 15–25 feet, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Intermediate Obedience Test
lessons.goal: Assess your dog’s mastery of intermediate-level obedience skills and readiness for advanced training.
steps: Sit-Stay (30–60 sec): Dog should hold a sit-stay reliably for at least 30–60 seconds, despite mild distractions.
Down-Stay (30–60 sec): Dog maintains a calm down-stay position for at least 30–60 seconds with mild distractions.
Reliable Recall: Dog responds immediately and promptly returns when recalled from 20–25 feet away.
Heel Command: Dog confidently walks at your side in a proper heel position for at least 15 steps.
Ignore Distractions: Dog remains focused and calm when exposed to moderate distractions.
Stand-Stay: Dog holds a stand-stay position reliably for at least 20 seconds.
tips: Perform the test in a controlled environment to ensure clear evaluation.
Reward generously after each successful assessment criterion to reinforce positive experiences.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog successfully passes all assessment criteria, reliably completing each skill at least 8 out of 10 attempts.

courses.title: Reliable Recall
courses.description: Ensure your dog always returns, even with distractions.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Recall Foundation
lessons.goal: Establish a clear and reliable recall command that your dog responds to immediately.
steps: Choose a Cue Word: Pick a distinct recall cue like “Come!” or “Here!”
Short Distance Practice: Begin indoors or in a quiet area at close distances (3–5 feet). Say the cue enthusiastically.
Immediate Reward: Reward your dog immediately with treats and praise when they respond promptly.
Repeat Regularly: Consistently practice in short sessions, gradually building reliability.
tips: Always use a happy and encouraging tone.
Ensure each recall ends positively, with praise or treats.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably comes immediately when called from short distances, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Recall with Minor Distractions
lessons.goal: Improve recall reliability when your dog faces mild distractions.
steps: Establish Calm Environment: Start recall practice indoors or in a quiet outdoor area.
Introduce Mild Distractions: Place mild distractions nearby, such as toys or familiar people.
Recall Command: Clearly call your dog using your established recall cue.
Reward Immediate Response: Generously praise and reward your dog when they return quickly, even with distractions nearby.
tips: Slowly increase the difficulty level of distractions.
Always reward immediately to reinforce prompt responses.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently responds promptly despite mild distractions, achieving success in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Emergency Recall Word
lessons.goal: Teach your dog a distinct and highly reliable emergency recall command for urgent situations.
steps: Select Unique Cue: Choose a unique word or phrase (e.g., “Now!” or “Emergency!”) distinct from everyday commands.
High-Value Rewards: Use exceptionally high-value rewards reserved solely for this cue.
Immediate Response Training: Practice at short distances without distractions, rewarding instantly every time your dog responds.
Increase Difficulty: Gradually increase the distance and introduce minor distractions while consistently rewarding prompt responses.
tips: Keep this cue highly positive and rewarding.
Practice regularly but sparingly to maintain its special significance.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog immediately returns upon hearing the emergency recall word, even with moderate distractions, in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Long-Leash Recall Training
lessons.goal: Safely practice and enhance recall reliability at extended distances using a long leash.
steps: Long-Leash Setup: Use a 15–30-foot leash in a safe, open environment.
Distance Recall: Clearly call your dog using your standard recall cue from progressively greater distances.
Consistent Rewarding: Reward your dog generously upon return each time to reinforce behavior.
Practice Regularly: Gradually vary environments and distances for increased reliability.
tips: Keep sessions positive and short, reinforcing success consistently.
Gradually phase out leash reliance once reliability improves.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably returns promptly from longer distances (20–30 feet) in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Recall During Play
lessons.goal: Train your dog to reliably return to you even during active play sessions.
steps: Start Play Session: Engage your dog in their favorite game or playful activity.
Introduce Recall Cue: Call your dog clearly using your recall cue during moments of moderate excitement.
Reward Generously: Provide immediate high-value rewards and praise when your dog returns quickly.
Gradually Increase Play Intensity: Slowly practice recall at more intense moments of play.
tips: Initially call your dog during slight pauses in play.
Always allow play to resume after successful recall, keeping it enjoyable.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently recalls promptly during play, responding reliably in 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Food & Toy Distraction Recall
lessons.goal: Achieve reliable recall responses even when your dog faces highly tempting distractions like food or toys.
steps: Controlled Setup: Place high-value distractions (favorite toys or treats) in controlled areas.
Recall Training: Clearly call your dog away from the distraction using your standard recall cue.
Immediate Reward: Reward immediately with something equally or more valuable to reinforce returning.
Gradually Increase Difficulty: Intensify distractions progressively while maintaining prompt recall.
tips: Initially use distractions that are slightly less appealing to ensure success.
Always reward your dog immediately upon returning, reinforcing correct behavior strongly.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently returns promptly despite strong distractions, successfully responding in 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Recall Around Other Dogs
lessons.goal: Train your dog to reliably come when called, even when other dogs are present.
steps: Controlled Environment: Begin practice at a safe, comfortable distance from other calm dogs.
Recall Command: Clearly call your dog using your established recall cue.
Reward Focus: Immediately praise and reward your dog when they promptly return, ignoring other dogs.
Gradually Increase Proximity: Slowly practice recall closer to other dogs, ensuring consistent success before moving closer.
tips: Use high-value treats or toys to reinforce correct responses.
Regular short sessions help your dog maintain focus and responsiveness.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably recalls despite the presence of other dogs, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Outdoor Recall in Open Spaces
lessons.goal: Achieve consistent and prompt recall responses in open outdoor environments.
steps: Long-Line Safety: Initially practice recall using a long leash (20–30 feet) in an open, secure area.
Clear Command: Clearly call your dog using your recall cue.
Immediate Reward: Generously praise and reward upon successful return.
Gradual Freedom: Progress to practicing recall off-leash in safe, fenced-in open spaces, maintaining consistent rewards.
tips: Ensure high-value rewards to encourage enthusiastic returns.
Keep sessions brief and positive.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently recalls promptly in open outdoor areas in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Immediate Stop and Recall
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to quickly stop any current action and promptly return upon hearing combined commands.
steps: Introduce Stop Cue: First, practice the "Stop" or "Wait" command separately at short distances.
Combine Commands: Once your dog reliably stops, immediately give your recall cue (“Come!”).
Reward Immediate Response: Reward generously when your dog stops and returns immediately.
Gradual Progression: Gradually increase distance and distractions, reinforcing consistent responses.
tips: Use a clear, firm tone for the stop command, and cheerful encouragement for recall.
Regular, brief sessions improve reliability.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably stops and immediately returns upon command in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Hidden Handler Recall
lessons.goal: Train your dog to confidently find and return to you when you are briefly out of sight.
steps: Start with Partial Visibility: Initially hide partially behind an object or corner, calling your dog clearly.
Reward Prompt Returns: Immediately reward your dog upon finding you.
Increase Difficulty Gradually: Slowly increase your hiding distance and fully conceal yourself, consistently rewarding upon return.
Regular Practice: Vary hiding places to generalize recall success.
tips: Begin in familiar environments to boost your dog's confidence.
Maintain excitement and rewards high to encourage enthusiasm.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently locates and returns to you when hidden, succeeding in 8 out of 10 trials.

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Proofing Your Recall
lessons.goal: Test and reinforce your dog’s recall reliability under varied conditions and higher-level distractions.
steps: Varied Environments: Practice recall in different locations (parks, yards, indoors, etc.).
Increase Distraction Levels: Gradually introduce higher-level distractions like unfamiliar people, toys, or food.
Consistent Rewards: Generously reward prompt returns, especially under difficult circumstances.
Evaluate and Reinforce: Regularly evaluate and reinforce any weaker recall responses to ensure consistency.
tips: Practice recall frequently but briefly to maintain enthusiasm.
Immediately address inconsistencies with extra practice sessions.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably returns immediately despite varied distractions, achieving success in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Reliable Recall Graduation
lessons.goal: Perform a final evaluation demonstrating your dog’s mastery of the recall command under multiple challenging scenarios.
steps: Distance Recall (30–40 ft.): Dog must promptly return when called from long distances.
Recall with High-Level Distractions: Successfully respond despite attractive distractions such as food, toys, or dogs.
Hidden Handler Recall: Locate handler swiftly when handler is hidden.
Combined Commands (Stop & Recall): Dog immediately stops current activity and returns when commanded.
tips: Ensure each scenario is clearly controlled for safety and accurate evaluation.
Reward generously during and after evaluation to reinforce mastery positively.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently demonstrates reliable recall mastery in all evaluation scenarios, successfully completing at least 8 out of 10 attempts in each scenario.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Leash Introduction
lessons.goal: Help your dog become comfortable and calm wearing a leash.
steps: Positive Association: Allow your dog to sniff and explore the leash; reward with praise and treats.
Gentle Attachment: Attach leash gently to your dog’s collar/harness for brief periods, immediately rewarding calm behavior.
Short Practice: Let your dog briefly wear the leash indoors, encouraging relaxed behavior through consistent rewards.
Frequent Sessions: Regularly practice brief leash-wearing sessions, gradually increasing the duration.
tips: Ensure sessions remain short, calm, and positive.
Avoid forcing the leash on if your dog seems stressed; slow down and reward often.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog remains calm and comfortable wearing the leash consistently over several sessions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Basic Leash Manners
lessons.goal: Teach your dog foundational manners to walk gently without pulling.
steps: Short Sessions: Begin leash training indoors or in a quiet, familiar outdoor area.
Gentle Guidance: Walk slowly, rewarding your dog immediately whenever the leash remains loose and relaxed.
Stop When Pulled: If your dog pulls, calmly stop and wait until the leash slackens before resuming movement.
Consistent Reinforcement: Regularly reinforce calm and gentle walking behavior with praise and treats.
tips: Maintain patience, consistently rewarding calm behavior.
Short, frequent training sessions enhance success.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently maintains relaxed leash manners, avoiding pulling in 8 out of 10 walking attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Stop-and-Go Technique
lessons.goal: Effectively teach your dog to avoid leash pulling using the stop-and-go method.
steps: Begin Walking: Start walking slowly with your dog on-leash.
Immediate Stop: As soon as your dog begins to pull, immediately stop and calmly stand still.
Wait for Relaxation: Wait patiently until your dog relaxes and returns attention to you.
Reward and Resume: Once the leash loosens, reward your dog and gently resume walking forward.
tips: Consistency is key; repeat each time your dog pulls.
Practice frequently to build reliable habits.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently responds to the stop-and-go technique, maintaining a loose leash during 8 out of 10 walks.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Changing Directions
lessons.goal: Improve your dog’s leash manners and attentiveness by frequently changing walking directions.
steps: Controlled Walk: Start walking slowly with your dog on a loose leash.
Sudden Direction Changes: Gently and frequently change direction, encouraging your dog to pay attention and follow.
Reward Attention: Immediately reward your dog whenever they quickly adjust to your directional changes.
Practice Regularly: Regularly integrate directional changes during leash walks, reinforcing attentiveness.
tips: Keep your movements gentle and calm.
Regular positive reinforcement strengthens attention.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably adjusts to directional changes, consistently maintaining a loose leash 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Maintaining a Loose Leash
lessons.goal: Consistently practice leash walking to maintain tension-free walks over extended periods.
steps: Set Clear Expectations: Begin walking calmly with a clear verbal cue such as “Let’s walk.”
Consistent Pace: Maintain a calm, steady pace and immediately reward your dog for consistent loose-leash behavior.
Immediate Correction: Calmly stop or redirect your dog gently if leash tension occurs, rewarding promptly upon relaxation.
Extend Practice: Gradually extend practice sessions, consistently reinforcing relaxed walking behavior.
tips: Use calm, consistent praise and rewards.
Short, frequent practice sessions reinforce reliability.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently maintains a loose leash for extended periods (5–10 minutes), successfully demonstrating this 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Ignoring Distractions
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to walk calmly on a loose leash despite minor distractions in the environment.
steps: Controlled Environment: Begin in a quiet area, gradually introducing minor distractions (e.g., toys, gentle sounds).
Gentle Walking: Start walking, encouraging your dog to stay near you with a relaxed leash.
Reward Focus: Immediately reward your dog for maintaining attention and ignoring distractions.
Gradually Increase Difficulty: Slowly introduce additional distractions or noises while reinforcing calmness consistently.
tips: Keep rewards frequent and high-value initially.
Maintain patience, ensuring gradual introduction of distractions.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably walks calmly and maintains focus despite minor distractions in 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Heeling Basics
lessons.goal: Introduce your dog to formal heel positioning, walking calmly beside you on a loose leash.
steps: Start in Position: Guide your dog into heel position at your left side, head aligned with your leg.
Begin Walking Slowly: Clearly give the cue “Heel,” then start walking slowly forward.
Immediate Reward: Consistently reward your dog immediately for maintaining correct position.
Practice Regularly: Frequently repeat short sessions, gradually extending heel walking duration.
tips: Use clear, consistent commands and visual cues.
Brief, frequent training sessions enhance skill retention.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably maintains correct heel position for at least 15 consecutive steps, succeeding 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Walking with Pace Changes
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to adjust smoothly and effortlessly to changes in your walking pace.
steps: Normal Pace: Begin walking at a comfortable, steady pace, maintaining a loose leash.
Introduce Pace Changes: Gradually increase and decrease your walking speed, rewarding your dog for smoothly adjusting their pace.
Immediate Reinforcement: Consistently reward your dog promptly for maintaining attention and leash manners during pace transitions.
Regular Practice: Incorporate varied pacing regularly to reinforce responsiveness.
tips: Keep initial pace changes gentle, gradually increasing difficulty.
Frequent rewards strengthen your dog’s responsiveness.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently and smoothly adjusts pace in response to changes during walks, succeeding 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Walking in Busy Areas
lessons.goal: Master calm and controlled leash walking in crowded, noisy, or busy environments.
steps: Controlled Exposure: Initially practice in moderately busy settings, gradually increasing crowd density.
Maintain Calmness: Use frequent treats and calm praise to reinforce your dog’s focus and relaxed leash walking.
Regular Rewards: Immediately reward your dog whenever they stay calm despite surrounding activity.
Consistent Practice: Gradually expose your dog to busier environments, reinforcing consistent calm behavior.
tips: Keep sessions brief and positive to avoid stress.
Gradual introduction of busy environments builds confidence.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably maintains calm, loose-leash walking behavior in busy areas, successfully demonstrating this 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Loose-Leash Mastery Test
lessons.goal: Evaluate and confirm your dog’s mastery of calm, controlled, loose-leash walking in various realistic scenarios.
steps: Consistent Loose Leash: Dog maintains relaxed leash tension throughout the test.
Heel Positioning: Demonstrate reliable heel walking for extended distances.
Pace Adjustments: Smoothly adjust walking pace without tension or pulling.
Ignoring Distractions: Remain calm and attentive despite varied distractions.
Busy Environment: Demonstrate calm walking in busy, crowded settings.
tips: Ensure high-value rewards to reinforce successful completion of each criterion.
Conduct test in multiple environments to confirm comprehensive mastery.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog successfully demonstrates loose-leash mastery across all criteria, reliably completing each scenario 8 out of 10 times.

courses.title: Fun Beginner Tricks
courses.description: Simple and fun tricks to engage your dog.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Shake Hands
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to politely offer their paw for a friendly handshake.
steps: Sit Position: Begin with your dog sitting calmly.
Introduce the Cue: Hold a treat in a closed fist near your dog's paw. Say "Shake."
Gentle Prompt: Your dog will naturally paw at your hand. When they do, gently grasp their paw, praise, and immediately reward.
Consistent Practice: Repeat frequently, gradually reducing the use of treats and relying more on praise.
tips: Be gentle and patient, rewarding each small success.
Short sessions keep your dog’s interest and enthusiasm high.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably offers paw upon hearing the cue “Shake,” succeeding 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Spin in a Circle
lessons.goal: Train your dog to make a simple, enthusiastic spin on command.
steps: Lure Technique: Use a treat to gently lure your dog into spinning in a full circle.
Introduce Verbal Cue: Clearly say "Spin" as your dog completes the motion.
Immediate Reward: Reward your dog immediately upon completing the circle, using praise and treats.
Repeat Regularly: Practice repeatedly until your dog reliably performs the spin on verbal cue alone.
tips: Keep movements smooth and gentle.
Gradually fade out treats, transitioning to verbal praise.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently spins in a circle upon hearing “Spin,” completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: High Five
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to enthusiastically give a "high five" upon request.
steps: Start with Sit: Have your dog sit comfortably in front of you.
Prompt Paw Lift: Place your open hand near their paw at chest height and say clearly “High Five.”
Immediate Reward: Reward immediately when their paw touches your open palm, pairing it with enthusiastic praise.
Consistent Practice: Gradually raise your hand position slightly higher, reinforcing consistent and enthusiastic paw lifts.
tips: Use upbeat, encouraging tones to enhance enthusiasm.
Practice briefly and frequently for the best results.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently performs an enthusiastic “High Five” in response to the cue, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Roll Over
lessons.goal: Train your dog to roll over playfully on command.
steps: Lie Down Position: Begin with your dog lying down comfortably.
Use a Treat to Guide: Hold a treat near your dog’s nose, gently guiding their head toward their shoulder, prompting a roll onto their side.
Complete the Roll: Continue the lure gently to encourage a complete roll, rewarding immediately once achieved.
Practice Regularly: Repeat consistently, pairing with the verbal cue “Roll Over,” gradually fading the lure.
tips: Keep the process gentle and patient; do not force the motion.
Short, frequent sessions ensure quick learning.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably completes a playful rollover on command, succeeding 8 out of 10 times.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Speak on Command
lessons.goal: Encourage your dog to bark gently on cue when prompted.
steps: Prompt Barking Naturally: Initially identify a situation that naturally triggers a bark (e.g., holding a toy or treat just out of reach).
Introduce Cue Word: Clearly say “Speak!” when your dog barks, then immediately reward with praise and treats.
Repeat and Reinforce: Consistently practice and reward gentle barking when prompted by the “Speak” cue.
Encourage Control: Reinforce gentle, controlled barking rather than excessive noise.
tips: Keep sessions short to avoid excessive barking.
Reward gentle barks immediately to reinforce desired volume.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably performs a gentle bark upon hearing “Speak,” succeeding 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Play Dead
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to lie completely still on their side as a fun, dramatic trick.
steps: Down Position: Start by instructing your dog to lie down.
Lure into Side Position: Using a treat, gently guide your dog’s head towards their shoulder, encouraging them to lie flat on their side.
Introduce Cue: Clearly say "Play dead" or "Bang!" as your dog settles into position.
Reward Stillness: Immediately reward and praise enthusiastically when your dog remains still for a moment.
tips: Stay patient, as lying completely still might initially be unfamiliar.
Practice consistently, keeping sessions positive and short.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably performs the “Play dead” trick on command, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Crawl
lessons.goal: Train your dog to crawl forward while staying low on their belly.
steps: Start from Down Position: Have your dog begin lying down comfortably.
Treat Luring: Place a treat near your dog’s nose, slowly moving it forward along the ground, encouraging gentle forward crawling.
Introduce Verbal Cue: Clearly say “Crawl” as your dog moves forward on their belly.
Reward Progress: Reward and praise every small forward movement, gradually extending the crawling distance.
tips: Keep your movements gentle and encouraging.
Short and frequent sessions are best.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably crawls forward several feet upon hearing the cue “Crawl,” successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Take a Bow
lessons.goal: Teach your dog to gracefully bow down, lowering their front half while keeping their hindquarters elevated.
steps: Stand Position: Start with your dog standing calmly.
Front-End Lowering: Guide a treat downward from your dog’s nose to between their front paws, encouraging a bow position.
Introduce Cue: Clearly say "Bow" as your dog lowers their front half.
Immediate Reward: Quickly reward your dog’s bow position to reinforce the trick.
tips: Reward quick, short bows at first, then gradually increase duration.
Maintain an enthusiastic and playful tone to encourage participation.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently performs a graceful bow on cue, successfully completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Jump Through a Hoop
lessons.goal: Introduce your dog to safely and confidently jumping through a hoop.
steps: Hoop Introduction: Allow your dog to calmly sniff and become familiar with the hoop.
Initial Jumping: Hold the hoop low to the ground, using a treat to gently guide your dog through.
Cue Word: Clearly say "Jump" or "Through" as your dog passes through the hoop.
Gradual Height Increase: Slowly raise the hoop, ensuring comfortable jumping height for your dog, rewarding each success generously.
tips: Always keep safety in mind; ensure jumps are gentle and stress-free.
Regular brief sessions build confidence.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog reliably jumps through the hoop at a comfortable height on cue, completing 8 out of 10 attempts.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Fun Tricks Showcase
lessons.goal: Combine all previously learned beginner tricks into a short, engaging routine.
steps: Sequence of Tricks: Create a simple routine combining 3–5 tricks (e.g., Shake, Spin, Play Dead, High Five, Crawl).
Smooth Transitions: Practice transitioning smoothly from one trick to the next.
Consistent Rewards: Immediately reward your dog after each trick during initial practice, gradually rewarding after sequences.
Performance Practice: Regularly practice the routine until your dog confidently performs tricks in sequence.
tips: Keep sessions short and enjoyable to maintain enthusiasm.
Use high-value rewards to motivate performance.
lessons.completionCriteria: Dog consistently performs a short sequence of beginner tricks smoothly and reliably, successfully demonstrating mastery 8 out of 10 times.
